concepts.title: Definition and Representation of Rational Numbers
concepts.definition: A number that can be expressed as a quotient of two integers where the denominator is non-zero.
concepts.key_idea: Any integer, fraction, or terminating decimal can be written with an integer numerator and non-zero integer denominator.

concepts.title: Closure Property of Rational Numbers
concepts.definition: The set of rational numbers is closed under addition, subtraction, and multiplication because performing these operations on rational numbers always yields another rational number.
concepts.formula: a + b in Q, a - b in Q, a * b in Q
concepts.key_idea: Combining rational numbers through addition, subtraction, or multiplication always produces a rational number, but division by zero is undefined.

concepts.title: Commutative Property of Operations on Rational Numbers
concepts.definition: Addition and multiplication of rational numbers are independent of the order of operands, whereas subtraction and division depend on order.
concepts.formula: a + b = b + a and a * b = b * a
concepts.key_idea: Reversing the order of terms does not change the result for addition and multiplication.

concepts.title: Associative Property of Rational Numbers
concepts.definition: Grouping three rational numbers in different combinations yields the same result under addition and multiplication, but not under subtraction or division.
concepts.formula: a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c and a * (b * c) = (a * b) * c
concepts.key_idea: Parentheses grouping can be shifted without changing the final sum or product.

concepts.title: Additive Identity Element Zero
concepts.definition: Adding zero to any rational number leaves the value unchanged, making zero the unique additive identity.
concepts.key_idea: Zero is the neutral element for addition across rational numbers.

concepts.title: Multiplicative Identity Element One and Reciprocals
concepts.definition: Multiplying a rational number by one returns the original number, and multiplying a rational number by its reciprocal yields one.
concepts.key_idea: One preserves identity under multiplication, while the reciprocal is the multiplicative inverse.

concepts.title: Distributive Property of Multiplication over Addition and Subtraction
concepts.definition: Multiplying a rational number by a sum or difference of two rational numbers is equivalent to multiplying each term individually and then combining them.
concepts.formula: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c and a * (b - c) = a * b - a * c
concepts.key_idea: Distribution allows expanding products of sums or factoring out common multipliers.
